title: jint_strict narrows json.Integer (i64) to i32 unchecked — values >= 2^32 silently truncate into valid small values, bypassing the ODN-5 fail-fast bar
detail: json.Integer is i64; i32(x) truncates (verified: i32(4294967396)==100, i32(4294967296)==0, i32(4294967297)==1). start_tick 4294967396 loads as 100, volume 4294967296 as 0, era 4294967297 as 1 — the surge fires ~2^32 ticks early instead of 'out-of-range values abort startup' (ODN-5). Negative-wrap fix (r1 #3) landed; positive coercion gap is new.
recommended_fix: In jint_strict, reject before narrowing: if x < i64(min(i32)) || x > i64(max(i32)) return 0, false. Add test rows for start_tick/volume/era = 2^32 and 2^32+100.

title: volume/multiplier/demand_weight have no upper bounds — i32 overflow in effective_volume is reachable from catalog data that passes the loader
detail: Verified: 2^30 * 4 wraps to 0 (spec silently never spawns), 2e9 * 2 wraps negative (vol <= 0 skip). A typo like volume 2000000000 with multiplier 1 spawns 2e9 packets/tick (OOM) instead of fail-fast. Same class: demand_weight > 2^31 in 2+ sinks makes weighted_pick's total exceed 2^32, biasing the Lemire draw.
recommended_fix: Add upper bounds at load (e.g. volume <= 1e6, multiplier <= 100, demand_weight <= 1e6) or compute effective_volume in i64 and reject products above max(i32) — fail-fast per ODN-5.

title: The new packet_types/demand json.parse value trees are never freed (no json.destroy_value anywhere) — odin test memory tracking flags leaks at the two new parse sites
detail: Each catalogs_load call leaks the parsed JSON value tree (maps at parser.odin:299). Base loaders (211/251/434) share the pattern; 3.1 adds two more sites and the 40-row fail-fast suite accumulates ~800KiB per test run. Bounded in the app/harness (one load per process), so no production consequence.
recommended_fix: json.destroy_value(v) on every exit path of each catalog block (or parse into context.temp_allocator so the harness's per-demo free_all reclaims it).
